newsitem.title: USA: Fla judge strikes some claims from tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Fla judge strikes some claims from tobacco suit.

text.p: A Florida judge Tuesday limited the ability of the plaintiff in a wrongful death lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co to present claims of fraud conspiracy against the tobacco company.

Circuit Judge Bernard Nachman ruled that lawyers for plaintiff Dana Raulerson will only be allowed to present claims of conspiracy to commit fraud pre-dating 1969, when federal cigarette package labelling laws were changed.

The ruling came a week before the scheduled start of trial in the lawsuit, in which Raulerson is suing R.J. Reynolds on behalf of the estate of her late sister, Jean Connor, who initially filed a product liability lawsuit but died of lung cancer in 1995, before the suit could be heard.
Nachman's ruling came on a motion for summary judgment by Reynolds which sought to eliminate plaintiffs' claims that tobacco companies had conspired to commit fraud.
Greg Maxwell, a lawyer for Raulerson, said the ruling would "narrow the scope of the evidence." But he said Raulerson still had a strong case and did not see it as a major setback.
Steven Werber, local counsel for Reynolds, said of the ruling that the company was "relatively pleased. We're happy to have what we have."

In granting a partial summary judgment, Nachman ruled that the plaintiffs' claims of fraud post-dating 1969 were preempted by a federal labelling law, the Public Health Cigarette Smoking Act, which was enacted at that time.
The law said that tobacco companies, after agreeing to put health warnings on cigarette packages, could not then be held liable for failing to warn customers.

"Here, Reynolds had no state law duty to disclose information to Ms. Connor other than the common law duty to warn," Nachman wrote. "Therefore, plaintiffs' concealment and non-disclosure theories are preempted."

Maxwell said evidence of tobacco company misconduct after 1969 could still come into play at the trial, during which lawyers for Raulerson will try to prove that tobacco companies perpetrated fraud by hiding the dangers of cigarette smoking.
R.J. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
